claims.text: Conventional EAM references inadequately represent the full range of atomic configurations in high-temperature ab initio HEA liquids.
Replacing an EAM reference with an on-the-fly MLIP trained on high-temperature ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch near HEA melting temperatures.
The proposed reference can be a neural-network potential or Gaussian Approximation Potential iteratively trained on diverse liquid-state ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations.
The method is applicable to both solid and liquid phases of high-entropy and analogous refractory alloys near their melting points.
Relevant refractory-HEA temperatures can exceed 1500 degrees Celsius.
Sampling diverse atomic configurations is critical near high melting temperatures.
An MLIP incorporating many-body interactions and continual updates from ab initio liquid configurations can bridge the structural complexity between the reference and ab initio target systems.
Training on a comprehensive set of liquid configurations enables the MLIP to capture the liquid's many local atomic environments better than a standard EAM.
Better representation of local atomic environments enhances phase-space overlap and reduces artificial integration-path mismatch.
The MLIP reference could reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 50% relative to conventional TOR-TILD EAM references.
Reducing integration-path mismatch will lead to more accurate free-energy calculations.
MLIP performance depends on the quality and representativeness of its training set.
Extreme compositions or rapidly changing configurations may challenge MLIP accuracy.

The hypothesis is falsified if the MLIP fails to decrease path mismatch by at least 20–30% or fails to move calculated free energies closer to a direct ab initio benchmark than the EAM reference does.
